scope: Explain confirmed interruption to committed user turn delay; reject unsafe endpoint shortcuts.
outcome: No production timing change. Added six boundary regressions; the observed 1.7 s remainder belongs to existing semantic endpoint protection, not a second post-cancel timer.
real_rtc_evidence_source: pause-continuation-recovery.json; same final three RTC cases from 2026-09-08, not a new RTC run
mechanism: Channel completed-text EOT returns about 0.424, below 0.5. Normal interruption uses stable substantive evidence and cancels old output; it does not change that EOT result into turn-complete evidence.
Installed LiveKit Agents 1.7.1 chooses the existing maximum endpointing delay of 3 s for a below-threshold result.
SDK speech-end anchor subtracts VAD silence_duration and inference_duration from the stop-event time. Its endpoint task sleeps only the remaining delay from that anchor.
With roughly 500 ms VAD silence, the remaining wait measured from VAD stop is about 2500 ms. Cancel at about 803 ms leaves about 1698 ms to commit.
The scripted VAD .2/.5 s and EOT .424/.95 controls confirm the anchor and fast path through real AgentSession and Channel orchestration.

negative_control.change: Test-only public AgentSession.update_options(endpointing_opts={max_delay: 1.5}); no SDK monkeypatch or production configuration edit.
negative_control.scenario: Model-boundary score .424, old output cancelled, next speech starts 1.6 s after VAD stop; following clause raises score to .95.
negative_control.result: Both original-policy cases pass. Shorter-maximum control commits the unfinished prefix in both cases before continuation.
negative_control.interpretation: Counterexample to treating accepted interruption as completed turn or shortening a generic uncertain-turn timeout; does not prove the default 3 s is globally optimal.

limits: New framework regressions inject EOT at the Channel model boundary; they isolate scheduling and are not end-to-end real recognizer or real-model accuracy tests.
Eight hand-selected text pairs are a diagnostic probe, not a representative evaluation set or calibrated error rate; score ranges overlap across intended complete/incomplete labels.
No claim that existing EOT inference milliseconds cover all EOT latency or that model-quality changes have been implemented.
The original physical-device and 3.75/3.85 s response-latency gaps remain. No deployment or new physical speaker measurement.
